name: First Light Brief — hourly
prompt:
Refresh Riley's First Light Brief and write it into the artifact database. This runs hourly, so be quick and cheap — no deliverable file, no long report. The only output that matters is the database write.

Artifact URL: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/428a6851-8f8f-4bbb-bdff-f1cedb5f694c

Riley is in Victoria, BC (America/Vancouver). Work in his local time.

FIRST, decide the shape of the run.
- WEEKDAY (Mon–Fri): full refresh, everything below.
- WEEKEND (Sat–Sun): SKIP GitHub and Railway entirely (send empty arrays), skip meeting-prep flags, never mark a task "Deep work", and prefer errands, family, house and personal items when trimming.

STEP 1 — Gather. Run these in parallel.
- Google Calendar: list_events for today and tomorrow, primary calendar, timeZone America/Vancouver, orderBy startTime.
- Google Tasks: list_task_lists, then:
  - OPEN tasks — list_tasks with showCompleted=false on "Today", "Short-Term Tasks" and "Waiting". Keep each task's `id` and its list's `id`; the page needs both to write completions back. Keep each Waiting task's `updated` timestamp for age.
  - COMPLETED TODAY — list_tasks on "Today" and "Short-Term Tasks" with showCompleted=true, showHidden=true, and completedMin set to local midnight in Victoria as an RFC3339 UTC timestamp (today at 07:00Z during PDT, 08:00Z during PST). These fill the "Completed today" column.
- Gmail: search_threads with query `in:inbox is:unread category:primary newer_than:3d`, pageSize 15. The `category:primary` filter is REQUIRED — Riley does not want Promotions, Social, Updates or Forums mail on this page, ever. Nothing returned means the Mail card is empty, which is correct. Do not widen the query.
- Readwise: readwise_get_daily_review, pick ONE highlight worth re-reading, preferring under ~200 characters.
- Readwise Reader: reader_list_documents, location "later" (or "shortlist" if empty), category "article". At most ONE article that fits today. If nothing fits, omit `reading`.
- WEEKDAYS ONLY — GitHub: search_pull_requests `is:open involves:rileytrottier23`, plus anything assigned to him. Only what is genuinely waiting on HIM.
- WEEKDAYS ONLY — Railway: list-projects, then get-status on each. Report a service ONLY if its latest deployment is not SUCCESS or the environment has undeployed staged changes. A healthy project produces an empty array and the card stays hidden.

STEP 2 — Judge, for the CURRENT TIME OF DAY. This is an hourly refresh, not a morning-only one: at 09:00 the headline is about the day ahead, at 15:00 it is about what is left, at 21:00 it is about tomorrow. Say what genuinely matters right now in one sentence, max ~30 words, plain language, no motivational filler. Cross-reference: if an email unblocks a task, or an article pairs with one, put that in the note. Cut ruthlessly — don't dump lists.

STEP 3 — Write. Artifact tool, action "write_db", the URL above, db_op "set", collection "briefing", doc_id "current". Read it first with read_db and pass its version as if_version. Body:

{
  "generatedAt": "<current UTC time, ISO 8601>",
  "dateKey": "<today in Victoria, YYYY-MM-DD>",
  "dateLabel": "<e.g. Monday 14 September>",
  "headline": "<the sentence from step 2>",
  "footNote": "Refreshed hourly, 06:00–22:00 Pacific",
  "footStatus": ["<short status tokens, see below>"],
  "timeline": [ { "time": "09:00", "label": "Event name", "allDay": false, "past": false, "flag": "No agenda" } ],
  "tasks": [
    { "id": "<the Google task id>", "taskListId": "<the Google task list id>", "taskId": "<the Google task id>",
      "title": "...", "list": "Today", "due": "Due today", "focus": "Deep work", "note": "..." }
  ],
  "completed": [
    { "id": "<the Google task id>", "taskListId": "...", "taskId": "...", "title": "..." }
  ],
  "inbox":    [ { "from": "...", "title": "...", "note": "...", "url": "..." } ],
  "services": [ { "name": "...", "status": "Deploy failed", "note": "..." } ],
  "review":   [ { "title": "...", "repo": "owner/repo", "note": "...", "url": "..." } ],
  "waiting":  [ { "title": "...", "age": "21d", "note": "..." } ],
  "reading":  { "title": "...", "source": "...", "minutes": "3 min", "url": "...", "note": "..." },
  "passage":  { "text": "...", "cite": "Author · Title" }
}

Field rules:
- TASK IDS ARE CRITICAL. `id`, `taskId` and `taskListId` must be the REAL Google Tasks identifiers, and `id` must equal `taskId`. When Riley ticks a box on the page it calls Google Tasks `patch_task` with exactly these two values — a made-up slug breaks the write-back silently. Never invent them.
- `tasks` — at most 7 OPEN tasks, in the order he should do them. `due` renders amber, `focus` purple, `list` grey.
- `completed` — tasks completed today, title and ids only, newest first, at most 10. Do not add notes or tags; the card is a record, not a list of instructions.
- timeline — one compact strip. At most 4 entries, SHORT labels, no note field; fold detail into the label ("Squash with Kristen, 10:00"). 24-hour times, `past: true` for anything already finished, "All day"/"Tomorrow" with `allDay: true`. `flag` is the meeting-prep warning (weekdays only) — two or three words like "No agenda" or "You're organizing" on meetings today or tomorrow that Riley organizes or that have no agenda. Omit otherwise.
- inbox / services / review — empty arrays are correct and normal; those cards hide themselves. Never invent filler.
- waiting — under 8. `age` is days since that task's `updated` timestamp, like "21d"; omit under 2 days.
- footStatus — 1–3 short tokens for things checked with nothing to report, e.g. "5 Railway services healthy", "Review queue clear". On weekends just ["Weekend brief"].

STEP 4 — Roll the checkboxes over. Read "briefing"/"checks". If its "date" is not today's dateKey, set it to { "date": "<today's dateKey>", "done": {}, "reopened": {} }. If it already matches today, LEAVE IT ALONE — it holds Riley's in-flight ticks and overwriting it would undo them.

Then stop. Reply with one line: that the briefing was written, and the headline.
